extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, students or writers researching Stephen King and his writing craft
extracted.subtask_description: Using a Wikipedia biography and bibliography of Stephen King to learn about his career, influences, and the writing advice he has given (as referenced by interviews, essays, and his book On Writing). Useful for writers looking to study King's approach to craft and horror fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on 'the craft' (On Writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stephen King repeatedly foregrounds 'the craft' of writing, as collected in his book On Writing: A Memoir of the Craft and referenced across interviews and essays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly cites On Writing and many interviews about King's approach; implication for writers: study King's practical, craft-focused guidance (revision, habits, storytelling fundamentals) as a model. No explicit step-by-step rubric is present on this Wikipedia chunk — consult On Writing and the cited interviews for detailed prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful attention to opening sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: King (and commentators) emphasize spending extensive time on opening sentences — the page references articles such as 'Why Stephen King Spends 'Months and Even Years' Writing Opening Sentences'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical takeaway: prioritize and revise your first sentences/paragraphs heavily; openings are treated as crucial by King and commentators. The Wikipedia text only cites the idea (via article titles); read the original pieces for examples and techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write what scares you (subject-matter guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Referenced interviews and pieces (e.g., 'Write the Book That Scares You: An Interview with Colson Whitehead' cited alongside King) imply a recurring piece of advice associated with King: write the stories that genuinely frighten or move you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a creative-writing criterion: choose subject matter that provokes an authentic emotional response in you (fear, curiosity, obsession), which will translate to stronger, more compelling fiction. The Wikipedia chunk lists the source references but does not include the full explanatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horror-specific craft and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple citations reference King's role and commentary on horror (e.g., 'The 'Craft' of Writing Horror Stories', Danse Macabre), indicating substantive standards and techniques specific to horror fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers studying horror should consult the cited works and interviews for conventions King discusses (building dread, pacing, everyday detail grounding supernatural elements). This Wikipedia chunk enumerates sources pointing to those standards but does not itself detail them.
